label: Bansal S20
title: Persistent tramadol, buprenorphine or oxycodone with ventricular tachycardia
statement: Persistent prescription of tramadol, buprenorphine, or oxycodone to a patient with a medical history of ventricular tachycardia [100, 101]

source.document: Bansal N, et al. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care. BMC Med 2024;22:5, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Bansal N, Campbell SM, Lin C-Y, Ashcroft DM, Chen L-C. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care - a modified e-Delphi study. BMC Med 2024;22:5. doi:10.1186/s12916-023-03213-x

plain_summary: Tramadol, buprenorphine and oxycodone can affect the heart rhythm, which matters in a person who has had ventricular tachycardia.

medicine_groups.name: Tramadol, buprenorphine or oxycodone
medicine_groups.note: Count buprenorphine supplied for pain, including skin patches and Temgesic sublingual tablets. Exclude supplies for opioid dependence. If the product or reason for use is unclear, report at most a possible finding and ask whether the supply was for pain.

needs_facts.meets: A history of ventricular tachycardia recorded at any time

options.words: Diagnosed with ventricular tachycardia at some point
Clinical history confirms no previous ventricular tachycardia

needs_facts.what: Reason for the qualifying opioid course
needs_facts.meets: Use the answer for the opioid course named in the finding. Chronic non-cancer pain meets the indication requirement. Cancer pain, end-of-life care or another indication excludes that course. If the reason is unknown or the answer cannot be linked to this course, keep it possible unless another requirement is ruled out.

options.words: Cancer pain, end-of-life care or another indication

rule_for_models: For a patient over 18, confirm only when at least two distinct prescriptions for tramadol, buprenorphine or oxycodone for chronic non-cancer pain support an ongoing course of at least three calendar months and the history confirms ventricular tachycardia at any time. Cite the opioid supplies, their indication and the rhythm history. Assess cover from dates, quantities and directions including the final supply. Exclude dependence treatment, cancer pain and end-of-life care. An explicit history of no previous ventricular tachycardia excludes the finding unless a previous episode is documented. A normal rhythm test, another rhythm diagnosis or an unnamed fast rhythm alone leaves the history unknown. If any requirement is ruled out, report no finding. If the course could qualify but age, indication, duration or rhythm history is unclear, report a possible finding and ask for the missing information. If the indication could change the finding, name the opioid and dates of the course and ask for "Reason for the qualifying opioid course". Use the answer only for that course. If the reason is unknown or the answer could refer to another course, report only a possible finding unless another requirement is ruled out.
cannot_be_seen: Heart rhythm problems that were never recorded, the type and cause of the tachycardia, heart medicines supplied elsewhere and device treatment such as an implanted defibrillator unless documented, and whether the pain is cancer pain or end of life care.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm any history of ventricular tachycardia if it is unclear, and review the suitability of this opioid and whether a rhythm check is needed?
